title: The reverse test: do connected firms run faster as a group?
question: Do firms with each kind of connection get building permits faster than like firms without one, and by how much?
finding: Turned around, the answer is no. Of the 1,157 firms in the speed test, 348 have at least one recorded connection and 809 have none. The average connected firm beats like permits on 48% of its jobs; like firms in the same role without a connection manage 47% (no difference beyond chance). By kind of connection: registered permit consultants (29 firms), 46% against 48%, no difference beyond chance; firms whose staff gave to candidates (301 firms), 47% against 47%, no difference beyond chance; clients of registered lobbyists (21 firms), 51% against 46%, no difference beyond chance; gift givers (10 firms), 48% against 47%, no difference beyond chance; City vendors (60 firms), 49% against 48%, no difference beyond chance; firms in a case file or on the extra-scrutiny list (13 firms), 46% against 47%, no difference beyond chance. 18 of the connected firms are consistently faster and 28 consistently slower; among the 809 unconnected firms the counts are 42 and 65.
how: All 1,157 firms in the building-permit speed test are tagged with each kind of connection, as in the previous screen. For each kind, the firms that have it are compared with firms that have no recorded connection at all, role by role (contractor with contractor, architect with architect, and so on), taking each firm's share of jobs faster than the like-permit median as one observation. The difference is called beyond chance when it is more than 2.58 standard errors from zero (about 1% of the time by luck; 8 comparisons are made).  The day gap is the median, across the firms, of each firm's median days minus the median for its like permits.
limits: A group average hides individual firms in both directions, and connected firms are larger and do different work than unconnected ones, which the role-by-role comparison only partly removes. Permit consultants are hired for hard jobs, which would make them look slow, or for owners in a hurry, which would make them look fast; this test cannot tell which. Connections are exact name matches and are undercounted. A null result here does not clear any single firm, and a positive one does not accuse any.
